# create_html_artifact — one-pager output

## Purpose
This tool exists for exactly one job, and it is a narrow one: producing a static overview or summary of a larger, already-completed body of work, packaged as a shareable one-pager. Good examples of what belongs here: a finished report summarizing findings, a wrap-up of a multi-step task the user just finished with you, a consolidated view of results gathered across a conversation, or a polished recap someone could forward to a colleague without further editing. This is not a general-purpose "make it look nicer" formatter, and it is not a way to make any output feel more finished — most of what you produce in a conversation, including long or well-organized answers, should still just be a normal chat reply.

**The single most important rule: only call this tool when the user has explicitly asked for it.** Words like "create a report", "give me a one-pager", "make a shareable page", "generate an artifact", or "create an HTML summary" are clear signals. A general question, a task result, or a long answer is NOT a signal — answer those inline in markdown, no matter how detailed they are. If the user did not ask for this format, do not use it.

Three additional rules apply once the explicit-request gate is met:
1. Only for an overview or summary of a completed body of work. If the content you're about to generate is itself the primary deliverable — a single answer to a question, one example, one explanation — it does not qualify, even if it's long, even if it's detailed, and even if formatting it as a page would look good. Ask yourself: "is this a recap of work already done, or is this the work itself?" If it's the work itself, this tool is the wrong choice.
2. Static content only, with no exceptions. <script> tags and all inline event handlers are stripped automatically when the artifact is saved, so nothing you produce through this tool can ever actually be interactive, no matter how it's written — buttons won't click, forms won't submit, calculators won't calculate. If the user is asking for something that needs to actually work — an app, a calculator, a live dashboard, anything with real behavior — this tool cannot deliver that and you should use file generation instead, not this tool.
3. Never a substitute for a code snippet or a mermaid diagram, even when the underlying content happens to be HTML or CSS. If what the user actually wants is a code example, a template, a demonstration of how something is built, or a diagram of a flow or architecture, the right home for that is a fenced code block or a mermaid diagram directly in your chat reply — not this tool, even if you could technically wrap that same content in an HTML page.
When you're not sure whether a given request matches this purpose, the safe default is to not call this tool and just reply inline instead. It is far better to under-use this tool than to over-use it.

## Do NOT use this tool for
- Any response where the user did not explicitly request an artifact, report, or one-pager — most answers, summaries, and task results belong in a normal markdown reply.
- Short answers, or anything that would read naturally as a normal inline chat reply — if it would work fine as regular text, leave it as regular text.
- Code snippets, examples, templates, tutorials, or demonstrations of how to build something — this holds true even if the output would technically be a full, well-structured HTML page.
- Diagrams, flows, architecture sketches, or anything that is fundamentally a diagram rather than a document — use a mermaid code block for these instead.
- Anything interactive: forms, calculators, small apps, live dashboards, or any UI element that implies the user will click, type, or interact with it and expect a real response. Remember: this tool cannot produce working interactivity under any circumstances.

## When you do call this tool
- The tool call must be the last action you take in the turn — do not add more content after it. Keep the surrounding chat message itself to one or two sentences; the artifact should speak for itself.
- Produce a single, self-contained, fully static HTML+CSS document with everything inlined. Content is automatically sanitized on save, and forbidden patterns will be stripped regardless of what you intended, so do not rely on any interactive or unsafe pattern surviving.
- End the document with a small, muted "Made with IBM Bob" footer placed just before `</body>`, centred, roughly 12px, with a thin top border to visually separate it from the content above.
- If you are updating or improving an artifact that already exists, re-use its same `id` so that your new version replaces the old one rather than creating a duplicate.

## Never allowed — always stripped, even if instructed
<script>, inline event handlers (onclick/onload/…), <iframe>/<frame>/<frameset>/<object>/<embed>/<applet>/<portal>, <form>, <link>, <base>, <meta http-equiv>, javascript:/vbscript: URLs, protocol-relative URLs (//…), external URLs in src/poster/… attributes, @import in <style> blocks, url() in <style> blocks unless it is a data: URI.
<a href> to external sites is fine. Inline data: image URIs are fine.

## Design
Single column, max-width ~760px, centred. No animations, gradients, shadows, emojis, or decorative icons. SVG only for data visualisation.
Font: `-apple-system, "Segoe UI", system-ui, sans-serif`, ~14–15px, line-height ~1.6.
Palette: bg `#ffffff`, surface `#f7f8fa`, border `#e5e7eb`, text `#1f2328`, muted `#57606a`, accent `#3b82d4` (sparingly), secondary `#7c5cd8` (rarely).

# Mode Switching

You can switch between different modes using the switch_mode tool. Each mode provides access to different capabilities and tools optimized for specific types of tasks.

**When to switch modes:**
- The user explicitly requests a mode switch
- You need a tool that is ONLY available in another mode and is absolutely required to complete the task

**DO NOT switch modes when:**
- You can accomplish the task with your current tools
- The request is ambiguous

Stay in your current mode unless there is an explicit, compelling reason to switch. When in doubt, do not switch.

# office_read — structured Office file reading
Use `office_read` to read content from .docx, .xlsx, or .pptx files. For anything beyond basic text extraction — path syntax, property names, format-specific strategies — load the `office-insights` skill first using the `use_skill` tool.
Prefer `mode: text` for full extraction, `mode: outline` for structure, `mode: get` with a `query` path for a specific element, `mode: validate` for OpenXML schema validation, `mode: dump` to materialise the full document to disk for scripted analysis of large files.
**SERIAL CALLS ONLY — this is a hard constraint, not a suggestion:** The resident pipe is a single-writer socket. Never issue multiple `office_read` calls in parallel (in the same turn). One call, wait for the result, then the next. Parallel calls WILL crash the resident.

# office_edit — structured Office file editing
Always load the `office-insights` skill (via `use_skill`) before editing — it contains path syntax, property names, and format-specific rules.
**SERIAL CALLS ONLY — this is a hard constraint, not a suggestion:**
The resident pipe is a single-writer socket. Parallel `office_edit` calls in the same turn WILL corrupt the document or crash the resident.
**Use `operation:batch` when adding multiple elements (e.g. a full slide with shapes).** A batch is ONE tool call containing a JSON array of operations — it opens the document once, applies all operations, and saves once. This is faster and avoids the parallelism trap entirely.
Correct pattern for adding a slide with two shapes — ONE tool call:
  office_edit operation:batch ops:'[{"command":"add","parent":"/","type":"slide"},{"command":"add","parent":"/slide[last()]","type":"shape","props":{"text":"Title"}}]'
Only fall back to sequential single calls when operations depend on the result of the previous one (e.g. reading back a path before using it).

# glob — file search
Use `glob` to find files by name pattern (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.ts"). Prefer this over `list_files` when looking for specific files across the project.
Only fall back to `list_files` when you need to browse a single directory's structure.

# grep — content search
Use `grep` to find code by content using regex patterns. Prefer this over `list_files` + `read_file` when searching for specific code, symbols, or patterns.
Use `read_file` only after grep tells you which file and lines to look at.

For factual questions that require knowledge about IBM products, platforms, languages, commands, APIs, configuration, documented behavior, compatibility, or product-specific errors, consult IBM documentation before answering.
This includes technologies such as IBM i, IBM Z, z/OS, Db2, CICS, COBOL, JCL, RPG, AIX, and watsonx, even when the user does not explicitly say IBM.
For Bob(or IBM Bob) product questions, call `search_ibm_docs` directly with `library_name: "bob"`.
For other IBM products, first call `list_ibm_doc_libraries`, select the most relevant exact library name from its response, and then call `search_ibm_docs`. Do not invent or modify library names.
You may reuse a library name already returned in the current conversation for follow-up questions about the same product.
Base factual product claims on the retrieved documentation. If no suitable library or relevant documentation is found, say so rather than guessing.
Documentation lookup is unnecessary when the request is purely about code in the workspace and does not require IBM product knowledge.

# Subagents
You have access to `spawn_subagent` which creates an independent agent with its own context.

**Default: do the work yourself.** Most tasks are faster and cheaper without a subagent.
Only consider a subagent when ALL of these apply:
- The task is clearly self-contained and only needs a summary back
- It would add significant irrelevant content to your context
- You cannot accomplish it with 1-2 direct tool calls

Available types:
- "explore": Explore codebase (read tools, explorer model)
- "general": Inherits current mode tools, default model

**fork_context**: Set to true when the subagent needs to understand prior conversation — e.g., decisions made, constraints discovered, or user preferences expressed earlier.
Leave false (default) when the description alone is sufficient context.

Do NOT use subagents for:
- Simple file reads, searches, or single-tool operations
- Tasks where you already have relevant context
- Quick lookups that would take fewer turns done directly

# create_chart — chart output
Use the `create_chart` tool when the user asks for a chart or data visualisation.

## How it works
Call the tool with:
- `type`: one of LineChart | BarChart | PieChart | ScatterChart | RadarChart | BoxplotChart
- `title`: short human-readable title for the chart tile
- `props`: a JSON string of chart-specific props

The props JSON must be valid for the chosen chart type. Do NOT wrap it in a spec fence.
Example for BarChart:
{"xAxisData":["Jan","Feb","Mar"],"series":[{"name":"Revenue","data":[4200,5800,3900]}],"title":"Monthly Revenue"}

Activate the `create-chart` skill before building props to get the full per-type prop schemas.

1 | def chunk_text(text, chunk_size=1000, overlap=200):
2 |     """
3 |     Divide text into smaller overlapping chunks.
4 |     """
5 | 
6 |     chunks = []
7 | 
8 |     start = 0
9 |     text_length = len(text)
10 | 
11 |     while start < text_length:
12 |         end = start + chunk_size
13 | 
14 |         chunk = text[start:end]
15 | 
16 |         if chunk.strip():
17 |             chunks.append(chunk)
18 | 
19 |         start += chunk_size - overlap
20 | 
21 |     return chunks

Now I have a thorough picture of the entire project. Here is the complete analysis:

---

## IntelliOnboard — Full Project Analysis

### What is Already Implemented

The project has a solid, working **Python/FastAPI backend** with a clean service-layer architecture. Here's exactly what exists:

#### Core Infrastructure (`backend/services/`)

| File | What it Does |
|---|---|
| [`github_ingestion.py`](backend/services/github_ingestion.py) | Clones a GitHub repo via `git clone` using GitPython; skips if already cloned |
| [`repo_scanner.py`](backend/services/repo_scanner.py) | Walks the repo tree, counts files and extensions, ignores common noise dirs |
| [`file_extractor.py`](backend/services/file_extractor.py) | Reads all text-based source files (`.py`, `.js`, `.ts`, `.md`, etc.) + important config files into `{file, content}` dicts |
| [`git_history.py`](backend/services/git_history.py) | Fetches last 10 commits (`hash`, `author`, `date`, `message`) via `git log`; formats them as AI-readable text |
| [`chunker.py`](backend/services/chunker.py) | Splits documents into 1000-char overlapping chunks (overlap=200) |
| [`embedding_service.py`](backend/services/embedding_service.py) | Generates local embeddings with `sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2` |
| [`vector_store.py`](backend/services/vector_store.py) | Stores chunks + embeddings in a **per-repo ChromaDB collection** (persisted to `chroma_db/`); uses `upsert` |
| [`retriever.py`](backend/services/retriever.py) | Semantic search against a repo's ChromaDB collection, returns top-k matches with distance scores |
| [`llm_service.py`](backend/services/llm_service.py) | Calls **local Ollama (`llama3.2:3b`)** with a prompt; strictly context-grounded |
| [`onboarding_service.py`](backend/services/onboarding_service.py) | Builds a role-based 7-day onboarding prompt; normalizes role names |

#### API Endpoints (`backend/main.py`)

| Endpoint | What it Does |
|---|---|
| `GET /` | Health-check root |
| `GET /health` | Health-check |
| `POST /analyze` | Full pipeline: clone → scan → extract → chunk → embed → ChromaDB → git history |
| `POST /ask` | Semantic search → build context (code + git history) → Ollama LLM → answer |
| `POST /onboarding` | Role-normalized context retrieval → build onboarding prompt → Ollama → 7-day plan |

#### Installed Dependencies (notable)
- `fastapi`, `uvicorn` — API server
- `gitpython` — git clone
- `sentence-transformers` — local embeddings
- `chromadb` — vector store
- `requests` — Ollama HTTP client
- `networkx` — graph library (**installed but unused**)
- `ibm_watsonx_ai` — IBM watsonx SDK (**installed but unused**)
- `pandas`, `numpy`, `scikit-learn` — data tools (**installed but unused**)

---

### What is Missing

#### 1. No frontend at all
There is no `frontend/` directory, no React/Vue/Svelte app, no HTML UI. Everything is raw API-only.

#### 2. No `requirements.txt` / `pyproject.toml`
No dependency manifest exists in the `backend/` root (only the `.venv` itself).

#### 3. None of the 10 planned features are implemented
Zero services, endpoints, or logic exist for any of the features listed below.

#### 4. Shallow git analysis
`git_history.py` only fetches 10 commits and flat metadata — no file-level blame, no diff extraction, no per-file change frequency, no author contribution maps.

#### 5. No code structure / AST analysis
Files are treated as flat text. No parsing of classes, functions, imports, or dependencies — required for architecture graphs, impact simulation, and test gap detection.

#### 6. No graph/knowledge structure
`networkx` is installed but nothing builds a dependency or call graph.

#### 7. No streaming
All LLM calls are blocking (`stream: False`). No streaming responses to the client.

#### 8. No authentication, CORS, or environment config
No `.env` loading, no `CORS` middleware, no API keys/secrets management.

---

### Feature-to-File Mapping

Here is exactly what needs to be **created** or **modified** for each planned feature:

---

#### 1. 🧠 Repository Brain
*A unified knowledge graph of the codebase — files, functions, imports, dependencies.*

| Action | File |
|---|---|
| **Create** | `backend/services/code_parser.py` — AST parsing for Python/JS/TS to extract functions, classes, imports |
| **Create** | `backend/services/knowledge_graph.py` — Build + persist a NetworkX graph of file→function→import relationships |
| **Create** | `backend/routers/brain.py` — `GET /brain/{repo_name}` endpoint returning graph as JSON nodes/edges |
| **Modify** | `backend/main.py` — register the new router |
| **Modify** | `backend/services/github_ingestion.py` or `/analyze` — trigger graph build after ingestion |

---

#### 2. 🗺️ Interactive Architecture / Knowledge Graph
*Visualize the graph as an interactive diagram in the UI.*

| Action | File |
|---|---|
| **Create** | `frontend/` — React/Next.js app with a force-directed graph component (e.g. `react-force-graph`) |
| **Create** | `backend/routers/graph.py` — `GET /graph/{repo_name}` returning nodes+edges in a D3-compatible format |
| Depends on | Repository Brain (knowledge_graph.py) |

---

#### 3. ⏳ Codebase Time Machine
*Browse the codebase at any historical commit; diff between points in time.*

| Action | File |
|---|---|
| **Modify** | `backend/services/git_history.py` — add `get_full_history()`, `get_file_at_commit()`, `get_diff_between_commits()` |
| **Create** | `backend/routers/time_machine.py` — `GET /time-machine/{repo_name}/commits`, `GET /time-machine/{repo_name}/file?commit=&path=`, `GET /time-machine/{repo_name}/diff?from=&to=` |
| **Modify** | `backend/main.py` — register router |

---

#### 4. 💥 Change Impact Simulator
*"If I change file X, what else breaks?" — traces import/call dependencies.*

| Action | File |
|---|---|
| Depends on | `knowledge_graph.py` (Repository Brain) |
| **Create** | `backend/services/impact_analyzer.py` — graph traversal (BFS/DFS) from a changed file/function to find all dependents |
| **Create** | `backend/routers/impact.py` — `POST /impact/{repo_name}` with `{file_path, function_name}` payload |
| **Modify** | `backend/main.py` — register router |

---

#### 5. 🚀 AI First-Contribution Generator
*Suggest good first issues/tasks for a new contributor based on repo state.*

| Action | File |
|---|---|
| **Create** | `backend/services/contribution_service.py` — prompt engineering around TODOs, simple functions, missing tests, small isolated modules |
| **Create** | `backend/routers/contributions.py` — `POST /first-contribution` with `{repo_name, skill_level}` |
| **Modify** | `backend/services/llm_service.py` — add a `generate_with_system_prompt()` variant for structured output |
| **Modify** | `backend/main.py` — register router |

---

#### 6. 🎓 Personalized Adaptive Onboarding
*Enhance the existing `/onboarding` beyond a generic 7-day plan — interactive Q&A, progress tracking, adaptive paths.*

| Action | File |
|---|---|
| **Modify** | `backend/services/onboarding_service.py` — expand role mapping; add skill-level-aware prompt variants; add follow-up question prompts |

===================================================================
--- file:///c%3A/Users/kaksh/OneDrive/Desktop/intelliboard/backend/services/code_parser.py
+++ file:///c%3A/Users/kaksh/OneDrive/Desktop/intelliboard/backend/services/code_parser.py
@@ -0,0 +1,238 @@
+"""
+code_parser.py
+
+Parses source files in a cloned repository to extract structural information:
+- Python files: full AST-based extraction (functions, classes, imports)
+- JavaScript/TypeScript files: regex-based lightweight extraction
+- All other supported text files: file-path-only records
+
+Returns structured, JSON-compatible data.
+"""
+
+import ast
+import re
+from pathlib import Path
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Constants
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+IGNORED_DIRS = {
+    ".git", "node_modules", ".venv", "venv",
+    "__pycache__", "dist", "build",
+}
+
+PYTHON_EXTENSIONS = {".py"}
+JS_TS_EXTENSIONS  = {".js", ".jsx", ".ts", ".tsx"}
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Python AST parser
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+def _parse_python_file(file_path: Path, relative_path: str) -> dict:
+    """Extract functions, classes, and imports from a Python source file."""
+    try:
+        source = file_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore")
+        tree   = ast.parse(source, filename=str(file_path))
+    except SyntaxError:
+        return _empty_file_record(relative_path, "python", error="SyntaxError")
+    except Exception as exc:
+        return _empty_file_record(relative_path, "python", error=str(exc))
+
+    functions = []
+    classes   = []
+    imports   = []
+
+    for node in ast.walk(tree):
+        # Top-level and nested functions
+        if isinstance(node, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)):
+            functions.append({
+                "name":        node.name,
+                "lineno":      node.lineno,
+                "args":        [a.arg for a in node.args.args],
+                "is_async":    isinstance(node, ast.AsyncFunctionDef),
+                "docstring":   ast.get_docstring(node),
+            })
+
+        # Classes
+        elif isinstance(node, ast.ClassDef):
+            methods = [
+                n.name for n in ast.walk(node)
+                if isinstance(n, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef))
+            ]
+            classes.append({
+                "name":    node.name,
+                "lineno":  node.lineno,
+                "methods": methods,
+                "docstring": ast.get_docstring(node),
+            })
+
+        # import X, import X as Y
+        elif isinstance(node, ast.Import):
+            for alias in node.names:
+                imports.append({
+                    "type":   "import",
+                    "module": alias.name,
+                    "alias":  alias.asname,
+                })
+
+        # from X import Y
+        elif isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom):
+            module = node.module or ""
+            for alias in node.names:
+                imports.append({
+                    "type":   "from_import",
+                    "module": module,
+                    "name":   alias.name,
+                    "alias":  alias.asname,
+                })
+
+    return {
+        "file":      relative_path,
+        "language":  "python",
+        "functions": functions,
+        "classes":   classes,
+        "imports":   imports,
+        "error":     None,
+    }
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# JavaScript / TypeScript lightweight regex parser
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+# Patterns – intentionally permissive to avoid false negatives
+_JS_FUNCTION_RE = re.compile(
+    r"(?:^|\s)(?:export\s+)?(?:async\s+)?function\s+([A-Za-z_$][A-Za-z0-9_$]*)\s*\(",
+    re.MULTILINE,
+)
+_JS_ARROW_RE = re.compile(
+    r"(?:const|let|var)\s+([A-Za-z_$][A-Za-z0-9_$]*)\s*=\s*(?:async\s*)?\(",
+    re.MULTILINE,
+)
+_JS_CLASS_RE = re.compile(
+    r"(?:^|\s)(?:export\s+)?class\s+([A-Za-z_$][A-Za-z0-9_$]*)",
+    re.MULTILINE,
+)
+_JS_IMPORT_RE = re.compile(
+    r"""^import\s+(?:.*?)\s+from\s+['"]([^'"]+)['"]""",
+    re.MULTILINE,
+)
+_JS_REQUIRE_RE = re.compile(
+    r"""require\s*\(\s*['"]([^'"]+)['"]\s*\)""",
+)
+
+
+def _parse_js_ts_file(file_path: Path, relative_path: str, language: str) -> dict:
+    """Extract basic structural info from a JS/TS file using regex."""
+    try:
+        source = file_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore")
+    except Exception as exc:
+        return _empty_file_record(relative_path, language, error=str(exc))
+
+    functions = [
+        {"name": m.group(1), "type": "function"}
+        for m in _JS_FUNCTION_RE.finditer(source)
+    ] + [
+        {"name": m.group(1), "type": "arrow_function"}
+        for m in _JS_ARROW_RE.finditer(source)
+    ]
+
+    classes = [
+        {"name": m.group(1)}
+        for m in _JS_CLASS_RE.finditer(source)
+    ]
+
+    imports = [
+        {"type": "import", "module": m.group(1)}
+        for m in _JS_IMPORT_RE.finditer(source)
+    ] + [
+        {"type": "require", "module": m.group(1)}
+        for m in _JS_REQUIRE_RE.finditer(source)
+    ]
+
+    return {
+        "file":      relative_path,
+        "language":  language,
+        "functions": functions,
+        "classes":   classes,
+        "imports":   imports,
+        "error":     None,
+    }
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Helpers
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+def _empty_file_record(relative_path: str, language: str, error: str = None) -> dict:
+    return {
+        "file":      relative_path,
+        "language":  language,
+        "functions": [],
+        "classes":   [],
+        "imports":   [],
+        "error":     error,
+    }
+
+
+def _detect_language(suffix: str) -> str:
+    mapping = {
+        ".py": "python",
+        ".js": "javascript", ".jsx": "javascript",
+        ".ts": "typescript", ".tsx": "typescript",
+    }
+    return mapping.get(suffix, "unknown")
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Public API
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+def parse_repository(repo_path: str) -> dict:
+    """
+    Walk the repository and parse every supported source file.
+
+    Returns:
+        {
+            "repository": str,
+            "files_parsed": int,
+            "files_skipped": int,
+            "parsed_files": [ { file, language, functions, classes, imports, error }, ... ]
+        }
+    """
+    repo = Path(repo_path)
+    parsed_files = []
+    files_skipped = 0
+
+    for path in sorted(repo.rglob("*")):
+        if not path.is_file():
+            continue
+
+        # Skip noise directories
+        if any(part in IGNORED_DIRS for part in path.parts):
+            continue
+
+        suffix   = path.suffix.lower()
+        rel_path = str(path.relative_to(repo))
+
+        if suffix in PYTHON_EXTENSIONS:
+            record = _parse_python_file(path, rel_path)
+            parsed_files.append(record)
+
+        elif suffix in JS_TS_EXTENSIONS:
+            lang   = _detect_language(suffix)
+            record = _parse_js_ts_file(path, rel_path, lang)
+            parsed_files.append(record)
+
+        else:
+            files_skipped += 1
+
+    return {
+        "repository":    repo.name,
+        "files_parsed":  len(parsed_files),
+        "files_skipped": files_skipped,
+        "parsed_files":  parsed_files,
+    }

"""
knowledge_graph.py

Builds a NetworkX directed graph from the output of code_parser.parse_repository().

Node types:
  - repository  : the root repository node
  - file        : every parsed source file
  - function    : a function or method inside a file
  - class       : a class definition inside a file

Edge types:
  - CONTAINS    : repository→file, file→function, file→class
  - DEFINES     : class→method (method is also a function node)
  - IMPORTS     : file→file/module (when the import target can be resolved)

Only relationships that can be derived from actual parsed data are added.
No relationships are invented.
"""

import re
from pathlib import Path, PurePosixPath
from typing import Optional

import networkx as nx

from services.code_parser import parse_repository


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Node-ID helpers  (keep IDs deterministic and URL-safe)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _repo_id(repo_name: str) -> str:
    return f"repo::{repo_name}"


def _file_id(repo_name: str, file_path: str) -> str:
    return f"file::{repo_name}/{file_path}"


def _func_id(repo_name: str, file_path: str, func_name: str) -> str:
    return f"func::{repo_name}/{file_path}::{func_name}"


def _class_id(repo_name: str, file_path: str, class_name: str) -> str:
    return f"class::{repo_name}/{file_path}::{class_name}"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Import resolution helper
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _resolve_import(module: str, current_file: str,
                    all_file_paths: set, repo_name: str) -> Optional[str]:
    """
    Try to map a Python or JS/TS import string to a known file in the repo.
    Returns the file_id string if resolvable, else None.
    """
    # Python: "from services.foo import bar"  →  services/foo.py
    # Python: "import services.foo"           →  services/foo.py
    # JS/TS:  "./utils/helpers"               →  utils/helpers.{js,ts,...}

    candidates = []

    # Convert dot-notation to path
    py_path = module.replace(".", "/")
    candidates.append(py_path + ".py")
    candidates.append(py_path + "/__init__.py")

    # JS/TS relative import  (strip leading ./ or ../)
    js_base = re.sub(r"^\.{1,2}/", "", module)
    for ext in (".js", ".jsx", ".ts", ".tsx"):
        candidates.append(js_base + ext)

    # Also try relative to the current file's directory
    current_dir = str(PurePosixPath(current_file).parent)
    for cand in list(candidates):
        candidates.append(f"{current_dir}/{cand}")

    for cand in candidates:
        # Normalise double slashes etc.
        clean = str(PurePosixPath(cand))
        if clean in all_file_paths:
            return _file_id(repo_name, clean)

    return None


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Graph builder
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def build_knowledge_graph(repo_path: str) -> nx.DiGraph:
    """
    Parse the repository and return a populated NetworkX DiGraph.
    """
    parsed = parse_repository(repo_path)
    repo_name = parsed["repository"]

    G = nx.DiGraph()

    # ---- repository root node ----
    root_id = _repo_id(repo_name)
    G.add_node(root_id, type="repository", label=repo_name)

    # Build an index of all known file paths (normalised with forward slashes)
    all_file_paths = {
        str(PurePosixPath(rec["file"]))
        for rec in parsed["parsed_files"]
    }

    for rec in parsed["parsed_files"]:
        file_path = str(PurePosixPath(rec["file"]))   # normalise separators
        lang      = rec["language"]
        fid       = _file_id(repo_name, file_path)

        # ---- file node ----
        G.add_node(fid, type="file", label=file_path,
                   language=lang, path=file_path)
        G.add_edge(root_id, fid, relation="CONTAINS")

        # ---- class nodes ----
        class_names_in_file = set()
        for cls in rec.get("classes", []):
            cid = _class_id(repo_name, file_path, cls["name"])
            G.add_node(cid, type="class", label=cls["name"],
                       file=file_path,
                       methods=cls.get("methods", []),
                       lineno=cls.get("lineno"))
            G.add_edge(fid, cid, relation="CONTAINS")
            class_names_in_file.add(cls["name"])

        # ---- function nodes ----
        for func in rec.get("functions", []):
            fnid = _func_id(repo_name, file_path, func["name"])
            G.add_node(fnid, type="function", label=func["name"],
                       file=file_path,
                       lineno=func.get("lineno"),
                       is_async=func.get("is_async", False))
            G.add_edge(fid, fnid, relation="CONTAINS")

        # ---- import edges ----
        for imp in rec.get("imports", []):
            module = imp.get("module") or imp.get("name") or ""
            if not module:
                continue
            target_id = _resolve_import(
                module, file_path, all_file_paths, repo_name
            )
            if target_id and target_id != fid:
                G.add_edge(fid, target_id, relation="IMPORTS", module=module)

    return G


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Serialisation helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def graph_to_dict(G: nx.DiGraph, repo_name: str) -> dict:
    """
    Convert the graph to a JSON-serialisable summary dict.

    Returns:
        {
            "repository": str,
            "summary":    { files, functions, classes, imports },
            "nodes":      [ {id, type, label, ...} ],
            "edges":      [ {source, target, relation} ]
        }
    """
    nodes = []
    for node_id, attrs in G.nodes(data=True):
        entry = {"id": node_id}
        entry.update(attrs)
        nodes.append(entry)

    edges = []
    for src, tgt, attrs in G.edges(data=True):
        entry = {"source": src, "target": tgt}
        entry.update(attrs)
        edges.append(entry)

    # Summary counts
    type_counts = {}
    for _, attrs in G.nodes(data=True):
        t = attrs.get("type", "unknown")
        type_counts[t] = type_counts.get(t, 0) + 1

    import_edges = [e for e in edges if e.get("relation") == "IMPORTS"]

    return {
        "repository": repo_name,
        "summary": {
            "files":     type_counts.get("file", 0),
            "functions": type_counts.get("function", 0),
            "classes":   type_counts.get("class", 0),
            "imports":   len(import_edges),
        },
        "nodes": nodes,
        "edges": edges,
    }


def graph_to_frontend_format(G: nx.DiGraph) -> dict:
    """
    Return a simplified nodes/edges dict suitable for D3 / react-force-graph.

    Nodes: { id, label, type }
    Edges: { source, target, label }
    """
    nodes = [
        {
            "id":    node_id,
            "label": attrs.get("label", node_id),
            "type":  attrs.get("type", "unknown"),
        }
        for node_id, attrs in G.nodes(data=True)
    ]

    edges = [
        {
            "source": src,
            "target": tgt,
            "label":  attrs.get("relation", ""),
        }
        for src, tgt, attrs in G.edges(data=True)
    ]

    return {"nodes": nodes, "edges": edges}

+    return f"repo::{repo_name}"
+
+
+def _file_id(repo_name: str, file_path: str) -> str:
+    return f"file::{repo_name}/{file_path}"
+
+
+def _func_id(repo_name: str, file_path: str, func_name: str) -> str:
+    return f"func::{repo_name}/{file_path}::{func_name}"
+
+
+def _class_id(repo_name: str, file_path: str, class_name: str) -> str:
+    return f"class::{repo_name}/{file_path}::{class_name}"
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Import resolution helper
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+def _resolve_import(module: str, current_file: str,
+                    all_file_paths: set, repo_name: str) -> Optional[str]:
+    """
+    Try to map a Python or JS/TS import string to a known file in the repo.
+    Returns the file_id string if resolvable, else None.
+    """
+    # Python: "from services.foo import bar"  →  services/foo.py
+    # Python: "import services.foo"           →  services/foo.py
+    # JS/TS:  "./utils/helpers"               →  utils/helpers.{js,ts,...}
+
+    candidates = []
+
+    # Convert dot-notation to path
+    py_path = module.replace(".", "/")
+    candidates.append(py_path + ".py")
+    candidates.append(py_path + "/__init__.py")
+
+    # JS/TS relative import  (strip leading ./ or ../)
+    js_base = re.sub(r"^\.{1,2}/", "", module)
+    for ext in (".js", ".jsx", ".ts", ".tsx"):
+        candidates.append(js_base + ext)
+
+    # Also try relative to the current file's directory
+    current_dir = str(PurePosixPath(current_file).parent)
+    for cand in list(candidates):
+        candidates.append(f"{current_dir}/{cand}")
+
+    for cand in candidates:
+        # Normalise double slashes etc.
+        clean = str(PurePosixPath(cand))
+        if clean in all_file_paths:
+            return _file_id(repo_name, clean)
+
+    return None
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Graph builder
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+def build_knowledge_graph(repo_path: str) -> nx.DiGraph:
+    """
+    Parse the repository and return a populated NetworkX DiGraph.
+    """
+    parsed = parse_repository(repo_path)
+    repo_name = parsed["repository"]
+
+    G = nx.DiGraph()
+
+    # ---- repository root node ----
+    root_id = _repo_id(repo_name)
+    G.add_node(root_id, type="repository", label=repo_name)
+
+    # Build an index of all known file paths (normalised with forward slashes)
+    all_file_paths = {
+        str(PurePosixPath(rec["file"]))
+        for rec in parsed["parsed_files"]
+    }
+
+    for rec in parsed["parsed_files"]:
+        file_path = str(PurePosixPath(rec["file"]))   # normalise separators
+        lang      = rec["language"]
+        fid       = _file_id(repo_name, file_path)
+
+        # ---- file node ----
+        G.add_node(fid, type="file", label=file_path,
+                   language=lang, path=file_path)
+        G.add_edge(root_id, fid, relation="CONTAINS")
+
+        # ---- class nodes ----
+        class_names_in_file = set()
+        for cls in rec.get("classes", []):
+            cid = _class_id(repo_name, file_path, cls["name"])
+            G.add_node(cid, type="class", label=cls["name"],
+                       file=file_path,
+                       methods=cls.get("methods", []),
+                       lineno=cls.get("lineno"))
+            G.add_edge(fid, cid, relation="CONTAINS")
+            class_names_in_file.add(cls["name"])
+
+        # ---- function nodes ----
+        for func in rec.get("functions", []):
+            fnid = _func_id(repo_name, file_path, func["name"])
+            G.add_node(fnid, type="function", label=func["name"],
+                       file=file_path,
+                       lineno=func.get("lineno"),
+                       is_async=func.get("is_async", False))
+            G.add_edge(fid, fnid, relation="CONTAINS")
+
+        # ---- import edges ----
+        for imp in rec.get("imports", []):
+            module = imp.get("module") or imp.get("name") or ""
+            if not module:
+                continue
+            target_id = _resolve_import(
+                module, file_path, all_file_paths, repo_name
+            )
+            if target_id and target_id != fid:
+                G.add_edge(fid, target_id, relation="IMPORTS", module=module)
+
+    return G
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Serialisation helpers
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+def graph_to_dict(G: nx.DiGraph, repo_name: str) -> dict:
+    """
+    Convert the graph to a JSON-serialisable summary dict.
+
+    Returns:
+        {
+            "repository": str,
+            "summary":    { files, functions, classes, imports },
+            "nodes":      [ {id, type, label, ...} ],
+            "edges":      [ {source, target, relation} ]
+        }
+    """
+    nodes = []
+    for node_id, attrs in G.nodes(data=True):
+        entry = {"id": node_id}
+        entry.update(attrs)
+        nodes.append(entry)
+
+    edges = []
+    for src, tgt, attrs in G.edges(data=True):
+        entry = {"source": src, "target": tgt}
+        entry.update(attrs)
+        edges.append(entry)
+
+    # Summary counts
+    type_counts = {}
+    for _, attrs in G.nodes(data=True):
+        t = attrs.get("type", "unknown")
+        type_counts[t] = type_counts.get(t, 0) + 1
+
+    import_edges = [e for e in edges if e.get("relation") == "IMPORTS"]
+
+    return {
+        "repository": repo_name,
+        "summary": {
+            "files":     type_counts.get("file", 0),
+            "functions": type_counts.get("function", 0),
+            "classes":   type_counts.get("class", 0),
+            "imports":   len(import_edges),
+        },
+        "nodes": nodes,
+        "edges": edges,
+    }
+
+
+def graph_to_frontend_format(G: nx.DiGraph) -> dict:
+    """
+    Return a simplified nodes/edges dict suitable for D3 / react-force-graph.
+
+    Nodes: { id, label, type }
+    Edges: { source, target, label }
+    """
+    nodes = [
+        {
+            "id":    node_id,
+            "label": attrs.get("label", node_id),
+            "type":  attrs.get("type", "unknown"),
+        }
+        for node_id, attrs in G.nodes(data=True)
+    ]
+
+    edges = [
+        {
+            "source": src,
+            "target": tgt,
+            "label":  attrs.get("relation", ""),
+        }
+        for src, tgt, attrs in G.edges(data=True)
+    ]
+
+    return {"nodes": nodes, "edges": edges}

"""
impact_analyzer.py

Analyses which files in a repository may be affected when a specified file changes.

Approach:
  - Uses the pre-built NetworkX knowledge graph.
  - "Direct dependencies" = files that the target file imports.
  - "Dependent files"     = files that import the target file (reverse edges).
  - Uses BFS to find transitive dependents up to a configurable depth.

Language note: no execution or runtime analysis is performed.
All results are labelled "potentially affected" — not "will break".
"""

from pathlib import PurePosixPath
from typing import Optional
import networkx as nx

from services.knowledge_graph import (
    build_knowledge_graph,
    _file_id,
)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

MAX_DEPTH = 4   # BFS depth for transitive search


def _normalise_path(file_path: str) -> str:
    """Convert backslashes and strip leading slashes."""
    return str(PurePosixPath(file_path.replace("\\", "/")))


def _collect_dependents(G: nx.DiGraph, target_fid: str, max_depth: int) -> list[dict]:
    """
    BFS on reversed graph to find all files that (directly or transitively)
    import the target file.
    """
    if target_fid not in G:
        return []

    visited   = set()
    queue     = [(target_fid, 0)]
    dependents = []

    while queue:
        node, depth = queue.pop(0)
        if depth >= max_depth:
            continue

        # predecessors in the original DiGraph = nodes that have an edge INTO node
        for pred in G.predecessors(node):
            pred_type = G.nodes[pred].get("type")
            if pred_type != "file":
                continue
            if pred in visited or pred == target_fid:
                continue
            visited.add(pred)
            edge_data = G.edges[pred, node]
            dependents.append({
                "file":     G.nodes[pred].get("label", pred),
                "relation": edge_data.get("relation", "IMPORTS"),
                "depth":    depth + 1,
            })
            queue.append((pred, depth + 1))

    return dependents


def _collect_dependencies(G: nx.DiGraph, target_fid: str) -> list[dict]:
    """
    Files that the target file directly imports.
    """
    if target_fid not in G:
        return []

    deps = []
    for succ in G.successors(target_fid):
        edge_data = G.edges[target_fid, succ]
        if edge_data.get("relation") == "IMPORTS":
            deps.append({
                "file":   G.nodes[succ].get("label", succ),
                "module": edge_data.get("module", ""),
            })
    return deps


def _file_symbols(G: nx.DiGraph, file_fid: str) -> dict:
    """Return the functions and classes defined in a file node."""
    if file_fid not in G:
        return {"functions": [], "classes": []}

    functions = []
    classes   = []
    for succ in G.successors(file_fid):
        node_type = G.nodes[succ].get("type")
        if node_type == "function":
            functions.append(G.nodes[succ].get("label", succ))
        elif node_type == "class":
            classes.append(G.nodes[succ].get("label", succ))

    return {"functions": functions, "classes": classes}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Public API
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def analyze_impact(repo_path: str, file_path: str) -> dict:
    """
    Build (or rebuild) the knowledge graph and return an impact report
    for the specified file.

    Args:
        repo_path:  Local filesystem path to the cloned repository.
        file_path:  Repository-relative path of the file being changed
                    (e.g. "services/foo.py").

    Returns a JSON-serialisable dict.
    """
    from pathlib import Path

    repo_name = Path(repo_path).name
    G = build_knowledge_graph(repo_path)

    normalised = _normalise_path(file_path)
    target_fid = _file_id(repo_name, normalised)

    # ---- Does this file exist in the graph? ----
    if target_fid not in G:
        # Try a case-insensitive / partial match
        lower_norm = normalised.lower()
        match = next(
            (n for n, d in G.nodes(data=True)
             if d.get("type") == "file" and d.get("path", "").lower() == lower_norm),
            None
        )
        if match is None:
            return {
                "repository":   repo_name,
                "target_file":  file_path,
                "found":        False,
                "message":      (
                    f"File '{file_path}' was not found in the parsed graph "
                    f"for repository '{repo_name}'. "
                    "Only Python and JavaScript/TypeScript files are currently parsed."
                ),
                "direct_dependencies": [],
                "potentially_affected": [],
                "symbols":      {},
                "limitations":  [
                    "Only .py, .js, .jsx, .ts, .tsx files are analysed.",
                    "Static analysis only — runtime behaviour is not considered.",
                ],
            }
        target_fid = match

    symbols      = _file_symbols(G, target_fid)
    dependencies = _collect_dependencies(G, target_fid)
    dependents   = _collect_dependents(G, target_fid, max_depth=MAX_DEPTH)

    # Build human-readable relationship descriptions
    explanations = []
    if dependencies:
        dep_names = [d["file"] for d in dependencies]
        explanations.append(
            f"'{normalised}' directly imports from: "
            + ", ".join(dep_names[:5])
            + ("..." if len(dep_names) > 5 else "")
            + ". Changes to the public API of those files may affect this file."
        )

    if dependents:
        dep_names = [d["file"] for d in dependents]
        explanations.append(
            f"The following files import from '{normalised}' and are potentially "
            "affected by changes to its public interface: "
            + ", ".join(dep_names[:5])
            + ("..." if len(dep_names) > 5 else "")
        )

    if not dependencies and not dependents:
        explanations.append(
            f"'{normalised}' has no detected import relationships. "
            "It may be an entry-point or standalone module."
        )

    return {
        "repository":   repo_name,
        "target_file":  normalised,
        "found":        True,
        "symbols":      symbols,
        "direct_dependencies": dependencies,
        "potentially_affected": dependents,
        "explanation":  explanations,
        "confidence":   "low-to-medium",
        "limitations": [
            "Only .py, .js, .jsx, .ts, .tsx files are analysed.",
            "Dynamic imports, monkey-patching, and runtime injection are not detected.",
            "Static analysis only — no execution is performed.",
            f"Transitive search is limited to depth {MAX_DEPTH}.",
        ],
    }

+  - "Direct dependencies" = files that the target file imports.
+  - "Dependent files"     = files that import the target file (reverse edges).
+  - Uses BFS to find transitive dependents up to a configurable depth.
+
+Language note: no execution or runtime analysis is performed.
+All results are labelled "potentially affected" — not "will break".
+"""
+

+    build_knowledge_graph,
+    _file_id,
+)

+
+MAX_DEPTH = 4   # BFS depth for transitive search
+
+
+def _normalise_path(file_path: str) -> str:
+    """Convert backslashes and strip leading slashes."""
+    return str(PurePosixPath(file_path.replace("\\", "/")))
+
+
+def _collect_dependents(G: nx.DiGraph, target_fid: str, max_depth: int) -> list[dict]:
+    """
+    BFS on reversed graph to find all files that (directly or transitively)
+    import the target file.
+    """
+    if target_fid not in G:
+        return []
+
+    visited   = set()
+    queue     = [(target_fid, 0)]
+    dependents = []
+
+    while queue:
+        node, depth = queue.pop(0)
+        if depth >= max_depth:
+            continue
+
+        # predecessors in the original DiGraph = nodes that have an edge INTO node
+        for pred in G.predecessors(node):
+            pred_type = G.nodes[pred].get("type")
+            if pred_type != "file":
+                continue
+            if pred in visited or pred == target_fid:
+                continue
+            visited.add(pred)
+            edge_data = G.edges[pred, node]
+            dependents.append({
+                "file":     G.nodes[pred].get("label", pred),
+                "relation": edge_data.get("relation", "IMPORTS"),
+                "depth":    depth + 1,
+            })
+            queue.append((pred, depth + 1))

def format_git_history(git_history):
    """
    Convert Git history into text that can be given to the AI.
    """

    if git_history.get("status") != "success":
        return "Git history is not available."

    commits = git_history.get("commits", [])

    if not commits:
        return "No Git commits were found."

    history_lines = []

    for commit in commits:
        history_lines.append(
            f"Commit: {commit['commit']}\n"
            f"Author: {commit['author']}\n"
            f"Date: {commit['date']}\n"

        )

    return "\n\n".join(history_lines)

def _run_git(repo_path: str, args: list) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
    """Helper: run a git command inside repo_path."""
    return subprocess.run(
        ["git", "-C", repo_path] + args,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        encoding="utf-8",
        errors="replace",
    )


def get_full_history(repo_path: str, max_commits: int = 200) -> dict:
    """
    Return up to *max_commits* commits with hash, author, date, and message.
    Suitable for the time-machine commits list.
    """
    result = _run_git(repo_path, [
        "log",
        f"-{max_commits}",
        "--pretty=format:%H|%an|%ad|%s",
        "--date=short",
    ])

    if result.returncode != 0:
        return {
            "status": "error",
            "message": result.stderr.strip() or "git log failed",
        }

    commits = []
    for line in result.stdout.splitlines():
        parts = line.split("|", 3)
        if len(parts) == 4:
            commits.append({
                "commit":  parts[0],
                "author":  parts[1],
                "date":    parts[2],
                "message": parts[3],
            })

    if not commits:
        return {
            "status":  "empty",
            "message": "No commits found in this repository.",
            "commits": [],
        }

    return {
        "status":       "success",
        "commit_count": len(commits),
        "commits":      commits,
    }

    """
    Return the list of files that were added, modified, or deleted in a

    """
    result = _run_git(repo_path, [
        "diff-tree",
        "--no-commit-id",
        "-r",
        "--name-status",
        commit_hash,
    ])

    if result.returncode != 0:
        return {
            "status":  "error",
            "commit":  commit_hash,
            "message": result.stderr.strip() or "git diff-tree failed",
        }

    files = []
    for line in result.stdout.splitlines():
        parts = line.split("\t", 1)
        if len(parts) == 2:
            status, path = parts
            files.append({"status": status.strip(), "file": path.strip()})

    return {
        "status":       "success",
        "commit":       commit_hash,
        "files_changed": files,
    }

    """
    Return the content of a specific file as it existed at *commit_hash*.

    result = _run_git(repo_path, [
        "show",
        f"{commit_hash}:{file_path}",
    ])

    if result.returncode != 0:
        stderr = result.stderr.strip()
        if "does not exist" in stderr or "exists on disk" in stderr or "Path" in stderr:

        "commit":  commit_hash,
        "file":    file_path,

    """
    Return the unified diff between two commits.

    """
    result = _run_git(repo_path, [
        "diff",
        from_commit,
        to_commit,
    ])

    if result.returncode != 0:
        return {
            "status":  "error",
            "from":    from_commit,
            "to":      to_commit,
            "message": result.stderr.strip() or "git diff failed",
        }

    # Build a lightweight per-file summary from the diff
    files_changed = []
    current_file  = None
    added = deleted = 0

    for line in result.stdout.splitlines():
        if line.startswith("diff --git"):

                    "deleted": deleted,

            current_file = parts[1] if len(parts) == 2 else line
            added = deleted = 0
        elif line.startswith("+") and not line.startswith("+++"):
            added += 1
        elif line.startswith("-") and not line.startswith("---"):
            deleted += 1

    if current_file:

            "added":   added,

        })

"""
impact.py – Change Impact router

Endpoint:
  POST /impact/{repo_name}   – analyse which files may be affected by changing a file
"""

from pathlib import Path

from fastapi import APIRouter, HTTPException
from pydantic import BaseModel

from services.impact_analyzer import analyze_impact

router = APIRouter(tags=["Change Impact"])

REPOS_DIR = Path("repos")


class ImpactRequest(BaseModel):
    file_path: str


@router.post("/impact/{repo_name}")
def get_change_impact(repo_name: str, request: ImpactRequest):
    """
    Analyse the potential impact of changing *file_path* within *repo_name*.

    Returns:
    - The target file and the symbols it defines
    - Files that the target file directly imports from
    - Files that import the target file (potentially affected)
    - A human-readable explanation
    - Confidence level and known limitations

    Note: all results are **static analysis only**.
    The word "potentially" is used deliberately — no runtime behaviour is inferred.
    """
    repo_path = REPOS_DIR / repo_name

    if not repo_path.exists():
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=404,
            detail=(
                f"Repository '{repo_name}' not found locally. "
                "Please call POST /analyze first."
            ),
        )

    if not request.file_path or not request.file_path.strip():
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=422,
            detail="file_path must not be empty.",
        )

    try:
        result = analyze_impact(str(repo_path), request.file_path.strip())
    except Exception as exc:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=500,
            detail=f"Impact analysis failed: {exc}",
        )

    # Surface a 404-style response if the file wasn't found in the graph
    if not result.get("found"):
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=404,
            detail=result.get("message", "File not found in the knowledge graph."),
        )

    return result

"""
time_machine.py – Codebase Time Machine router

Endpoints:
  GET /time-machine/{repo_name}/commits
      List full commit history (up to 200 commits by default)

  GET /time-machine/{repo_name}/file?commit=<hash>&path=<file>
      Retrieve a file's content as it existed at a specific commit

  GET /time-machine/{repo_name}/diff?from=<hash>&to=<hash>
      Get the unified diff between two commits
"""

from pathlib import Path
from typing import Optional

from fastapi import APIRouter, HTTPException, Query

from services.git_history import (
    get_full_history,
    get_file_at_commit,
    get_diff_between_commits,
    get_files_changed_in_commit,
    get_file_history,
)

router = APIRouter(tags=["Time Machine"])

REPOS_DIR = Path("repos")


def _repo_path(repo_name: str) -> str:
    """Resolve and validate the local repo path."""
    path = REPOS_DIR / repo_name
    if not path.exists():
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=404,
            detail=(
                f"Repository '{repo_name}' not found locally. "
                "Please call POST /analyze first to clone the repository."
            ),
        )
    return str(path)


def _git_error_or_result(result: dict, not_found_statuses=("not_found", "empty")):
    """
    Raise an appropriate HTTPException if the git operation returned an error.
    Returns the result unchanged otherwise.
    """
    status = result.get("status")
    if status == "error":
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=500,
            detail=result.get("message", "Git operation failed."),
        )
    if status in not_found_statuses:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=404,
            detail=result.get("message", "Not found."),
        )
    return result


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Endpoints
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

@router.get("/time-machine/{repo_name}/commits")
def list_commits(
    repo_name: str,
    limit: int = Query(default=100, ge=1, le=500,
                       description="Maximum number of commits to return"),
):
    """
    Return the commit history for the repository.

    Query params:
      - limit (int, 1–500, default 100): how many commits to return
    """
    repo = _repo_path(repo_name)
    result = get_full_history(repo, max_commits=limit)
    return _git_error_or_result(result, not_found_statuses=("empty",))


@router.get("/time-machine/{repo_name}/file")
def get_file_version(
    repo_name: str,
    commit: str = Query(..., description="Full or abbreviated commit hash"),
    path:   str = Query(..., description="Repository-relative file path"),
):
    """
    Return the content of *path* as it existed at *commit*.

    Query params (both required):
      - commit : git commit hash (full or abbreviated)
      - path   : file path relative to the repository root (e.g. "src/main.py")
    """
    if not commit.strip():
        raise HTTPException(status_code=422, detail="commit must not be empty.")
    if not path.strip():
        raise HTTPException(status_code=422, detail="path must not be empty.")

    repo   = _repo_path(repo_name)
    result = get_file_at_commit(repo, commit.strip(), path.strip())
    return _git_error_or_result(result, not_found_statuses=("not_found",))


@router.get("/time-machine/{repo_name}/diff")
def compare_commits(
    repo_name: str,
    from_commit: str = Query(..., alias="from",
                             description="Start commit hash"),
    to_commit:   str = Query(..., alias="to",
                             description="End commit hash"),
):
    """
    Return the diff between two commits.

    Query params (both required):
      - from : start commit hash
      - to   : end commit hash

    Response includes a structured per-file summary (lines added / deleted)
    and the full raw unified diff.
    """
    if not from_commit.strip():
        raise HTTPException(status_code=422, detail="'from' must not be empty.")
    if not to_commit.strip():
        raise HTTPException(status_code=422, detail="'to' must not be empty.")

    repo   = _repo_path(repo_name)
    result = get_diff_between_commits(repo, from_commit.strip(), to_commit.strip())
    return _git_error_or_result(result)


@router.get("/time-machine/{repo_name}/commit/{commit_hash}")
def inspect_commit(
    repo_name:   str,
    commit_hash: str,
):
    """
    Return the list of files changed in a single commit (bonus endpoint).

    Path params:
      - repo_name   : repository name
      - commit_hash : git commit hash
    """
    repo   = _repo_path(repo_name)
    result = get_files_changed_in_commit(repo, commit_hash)
    return _git_error_or_result(result)


@router.get("/time-machine/{repo_name}/file-history")
def file_commit_history(
    repo_name: str,
    path:  str = Query(..., description="Repository-relative file path"),
    limit: int = Query(default=50, ge=1, le=200,
                       description="Maximum number of commits to return"),
):
    """
    Return the full commit history for a single file (bonus endpoint).

    Query params:
      - path  : file path relative to the repository root
      - limit : max commits (1–200, default 50)
    """
    if not path.strip():
        raise HTTPException(status_code=422, detail="path must not be empty.")

    repo   = _repo_path(repo_name)
    result = get_file_history(repo, path.strip(), max_commits=limit)
    return _git_error_or_result(result, not_found_statuses=("not_found",))

from fastapi import FastAPI
from pydantic import BaseModel

from services.github_ingestion import clone_repository
from services.repo_scanner import scan_repository
from services.file_extractor import extract_files
from services.git_history import get_git_history, format_git_history
from services.chunker import chunk_documents
from services.vector_store import store_chunks
from services.retriever import search_repository
from services.llm_service import generate_answer
from services.onboarding_service import (
    generate_onboarding_prompt,
    normalize_role
)


app = FastAPI(title="IntelliOnboard API")


class AnalyzeRequest(BaseModel):
    repo_url: str


class AskRequest(BaseModel):
    question: str
    repo_name: str


class OnboardingRequest(BaseModel):
    role: str
    repo_name: str


@app.get("/")
def root():
    return {
        "message": "IntelliOnboard backend is running!"
    }


@app.get("/health")
def health():
    return {
        "status": "healthy"
    }


@app.post("/analyze")
def analyze_repository(request: AnalyzeRequest):

    repo_url = request.repo_url.rstrip("/")

    repo_name = repo_url.split("/")[-1]

    if repo_name.endswith(".git"):
        repo_name = repo_name[:-4]

    # 1. Clone repository
    result = clone_repository(repo_url, repo_name)

    # 2. Scan repository
    scan_result = scan_repository(result["path"])

    # 3. Extract files
    documents = extract_files(result["path"])

    # 4. Create chunks
    chunks = chunk_documents(documents)

    # 5. Store chunks in repository-specific ChromaDB
    vector_result = store_chunks(
        chunks,
        repo_name
    )

    # 6. Get Git history
    git_history = get_git_history(
        result["path"]
    )

    return {
        "message": "Repository analyzed successfully",
        "repository": repo_name,
        "clone": result,
        "scan": scan_result,
        "documents": documents,
        "chunks": chunks,
        "vector_store": vector_result,
        "git_history": git_history

    repo_url = request.repo_url.rstrip("/")

    # 2. Scan repository

"""
knowledge_graph.py

Builds a NetworkX directed graph from the output of code_parser.parse_repository().

Node types:
  - repository  : the root repository node
  - file        : every parsed source file
  - function    : a function or method inside a file
  - class       : a class definition inside a file

Edge types:
  - CONTAINS    : repository→file, file→function, file→class
  - DEFINES     : class→method (method is also a function node)
  - IMPORTS     : file→file/module (when the import target can be resolved)

Only relationships that can be derived from actual parsed data are added.
No relationships are invented.
"""

import re
from pathlib import Path, PurePosixPath
from typing import Optional

import networkx as nx

from services.code_parser import parse_repository


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Node-ID helpers  (keep IDs deterministic and URL-safe)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _repo_id(repo_name: str) -> str:
    return f"repo::{repo_name}"


def _file_id(repo_name: str, file_path: str) -> str:
    return f"file::{repo_name}/{file_path}"


def _func_id(repo_name: str, file_path: str, func_name: str) -> str:
    return f"func::{repo_name}/{file_path}::{func_name}"


def _class_id(repo_name: str, file_path: str, class_name: str) -> str:
    return f"class::{repo_name}/{file_path}::{class_name}"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Import resolution helper
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _resolve_import(module: str, current_file: str,
                    all_file_paths: set, repo_name: str) -> Optional[str]:
    """
    Try to map a Python or JS/TS import string to a known file in the repo.
    Returns the file_id string if resolvable, else None.
    """
    # Python: "from services.foo import bar"  →  services/foo.py
    # Python: "import services.foo"           →  services/foo.py
    # JS/TS:  "./utils/helpers"               →  utils/helpers.{js,ts,...}

    candidates = []

    # Convert dot-notation to path
    py_path = module.replace(".", "/")
    candidates.append(py_path + ".py")
    candidates.append(py_path + "/__init__.py")

    # JS/TS relative import  (strip leading ./ or ../)
    js_base = re.sub(r"^\.{1,2}/", "", module)
    for ext in (".js", ".jsx", ".ts", ".tsx"):
        candidates.append(js_base + ext)

    # Also try relative to the current file's directory
    current_dir = str(PurePosixPath(current_file).parent)
    for cand in list(candidates):
        candidates.append(f"{current_dir}/{cand}")

    for cand in candidates:
        # Normalise double slashes etc.
        clean = str(PurePosixPath(cand))
        if clean in all_file_paths:
            return _file_id(repo_name, clean)

    return None


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Graph builder
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def build_knowledge_graph(repo_path: str) -> nx.DiGraph:
    """
    Parse the repository and return a populated NetworkX DiGraph.
    """
    parsed = parse_repository(repo_path)
    repo_name = parsed["repository"]

    G = nx.DiGraph()

    # ---- repository root node ----
    root_id = _repo_id(repo_name)
    G.add_node(root_id, type="repository", label=repo_name)

    # Build an index of all known file paths (normalised with forward slashes)
    all_file_paths = {
        str(PurePosixPath(rec["file"]))
        for rec in parsed["parsed_files"]
    }

    for rec in parsed["parsed_files"]:
        file_path = str(PurePosixPath(rec["file"]))   # normalise separators
        lang      = rec["language"]
        fid       = _file_id(repo_name, file_path)

        # ---- file node ----
        G.add_node(fid, type="file", label=file_path,
                   language=lang, path=file_path)
        G.add_edge(root_id, fid, relation="CONTAINS")

        # ---- class nodes ----
        class_names_in_file = set()
        for cls in rec.get("classes", []):
            cid = _class_id(repo_name, file_path, cls["name"])
            G.add_node(cid, type="class", label=cls["name"],
                       file=file_path,
                       methods=cls.get("methods", []),
                       lineno=cls.get("lineno"))
            G.add_edge(fid, cid, relation="CONTAINS")
            class_names_in_file.add(cls["name"])

        # ---- function nodes ----
        for func in rec.get("functions", []):
            fnid = _func_id(repo_name, file_path, func["name"])
            G.add_node(fnid, type="function", label=func["name"],
                       file=file_path,
                       lineno=func.get("lineno"),
                       is_async=func.get("is_async", False))
            G.add_edge(fid, fnid, relation="CONTAINS")

        # ---- import edges ----
        for imp in rec.get("imports", []):
            module = imp.get("module") or imp.get("name") or ""
            if not module:
                continue
            target_id = _resolve_import(
                module, file_path, all_file_paths, repo_name
            )
            if target_id and target_id != fid:
                G.add_edge(fid, target_id, relation="IMPORTS", module=module)

    return G


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Serialisation helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def graph_to_dict(G: nx.DiGraph, repo_name: str) -> dict:
    """
    Convert the graph to a JSON-serialisable summary dict.

    Returns:
        {
            "repository": str,
            "summary":    { files, functions, classes, imports },
            "nodes":      [ {id, type, label, ...} ],
            "edges":      [ {source, target, relation} ]
        }
    """
    nodes = []
    for node_id, attrs in G.nodes(data=True):
        entry = {"id": node_id}
        entry.update(attrs)
        nodes.append(entry)

    edges = []
    for src, tgt, attrs in G.edges(data=True):
        entry = {"source": src, "target": tgt}
        entry.update(attrs)
        edges.append(entry)

    # Summary counts
    type_counts = {}
    for _, attrs in G.nodes(data=True):
        t = attrs.get("type", "unknown")
        type_counts[t] = type_counts.get(t, 0) + 1

    import_edges = [e for e in edges if e.get("relation") == "IMPORTS"]

    return {
        "repository": repo_name,
        "summary": {
            "files":     type_counts.get("file", 0),
            "functions": type_counts.get("function", 0),
            "classes":   type_counts.get("class", 0),
            "imports":   len(import_edges),
        },
        "nodes": nodes,
        "edges": edges,
    }


def graph_to_frontend_format(G: nx.DiGraph) -> dict:
    """
    Return a simplified nodes/edges dict suitable for D3 / react-force-graph.

    Nodes: { id, label, type }
    Edges: { source, target, label }
    """
    nodes = [
        {
            "id":    node_id,
            "label": attrs.get("label", node_id),
            "type":  attrs.get("type", "unknown"),
        }
        for node_id, attrs in G.nodes(data=True)
    ]

    edges = [
        {
            "source": src,
            "target": tgt,
            "label":  attrs.get("relation", ""),
        }
        for src, tgt, attrs in G.edges(data=True)
    ]

    return {"nodes": nodes, "edges": edges}

"""
knowledge_graph.py

Builds a NetworkX directed graph from the output of code_parser.parse_repository().

Node types:
  - repository  : the root repository node
  - file        : every parsed source file
  - function    : a function or method inside a file
  - class       : a class definition inside a file

Edge types:
  - CONTAINS    : repository→file, file→function, file→class
  - DEFINES     : class→method (method is also a function node)
  - IMPORTS     : file→file/module (when the import target can be resolved)

Only relationships that can be derived from actual parsed data are added.
No relationships are invented.
"""

import re
from pathlib import Path, PurePosixPath
from typing import Optional

import networkx as nx

from services.code_parser import parse_repository


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Node-ID helpers  (keep IDs deterministic and URL-safe)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _repo_id(repo_name: str) -> str:
    return f"repo::{repo_name}"


def _file_id(repo_name: str, file_path: str) -> str:
    return f"file::{repo_name}/{file_path}"


def _func_id(repo_name: str, file_path: str, func_name: str) -> str:
    return f"func::{repo_name}/{file_path}::{func_name}"


def _class_id(repo_name: str, file_path: str, class_name: str) -> str:
    return f"class::{repo_name}/{file_path}::{class_name}"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Import resolution helper
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _resolve_import(module: str, current_file: str,
                    all_file_paths: set, repo_name: str) -> Optional[str]:
    """
    Try to map a Python or JS/TS import string to a known file in the repo.
    Returns the file_id string if resolvable, else None.
    """
    # Python: "from services.foo import bar"  →  services/foo.py
    # Python: "import services.foo"           →  services/foo.py
    # JS/TS:  "./utils/helpers"               →  utils/helpers.{js,ts,...}

    candidates = []

    # Convert dot-notation to path
    py_path = module.replace(".", "/")
    candidates.append(py_path + ".py")
    candidates.append(py_path + "/__init__.py")

    # JS/TS relative import  (strip leading ./ or ../)
    js_base = re.sub(r"^\.{1,2}/", "", module)
    for ext in (".js", ".jsx", ".ts", ".tsx"):
        candidates.append(js_base + ext)

    # Also try relative to the current file's directory
    current_dir = str(PurePosixPath(current_file).parent)
    for cand in list(candidates):
        candidates.append(f"{current_dir}/{cand}")

    for cand in candidates:
        # Normalise double slashes etc.
        clean = str(PurePosixPath(cand))
        if clean in all_file_paths:
            return _file_id(repo_name, clean)

    return None


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Graph builder
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def build_knowledge_graph(repo_path: str) -> nx.DiGraph:
    """
    Parse the repository and return a populated NetworkX DiGraph.
    """
    parsed = parse_repository(repo_path)
    repo_name = parsed["repository"]

    G = nx.DiGraph()

    # ---- repository root node ----
    root_id = _repo_id(repo_name)
    G.add_node(root_id, type="repository", label=repo_name)

    # Build an index of all known file paths (normalised with forward slashes)
    all_file_paths = {
        str(PurePosixPath(rec["file"]))
        for rec in parsed["parsed_files"]
    }

    for rec in parsed["parsed_files"]:
        file_path = str(PurePosixPath(rec["file"].replace("\\", "/")))   # normalise separators
        lang      = rec["language"]
        fid       = _file_id(repo_name, file_path)

        # ---- file node ----
        G.add_node(fid, type="file", label=file_path,
                   language=lang, path=file_path)
        G.add_edge(root_id, fid, relation="CONTAINS")

        # ---- class nodes ----
        class_names_in_file = set()
        for cls in rec.get("classes", []):
            cid = _class_id(repo_name, file_path, cls["name"])
            G.add_node(cid, type="class", label=cls["name"],
                       file=file_path,
                       methods=cls.get("methods", []),
                       lineno=cls.get("lineno"))
            G.add_edge(fid, cid, relation="CONTAINS")
            class_names_in_file.add(cls["name"])

        # ---- function nodes ----
        for func in rec.get("functions", []):
            fnid = _func_id(repo_name, file_path, func["name"])
            G.add_node(fnid, type="function", label=func["name"],
                       file=file_path,
                       lineno=func.get("lineno"),
                       is_async=func.get("is_async", False))
            G.add_edge(fid, fnid, relation="CONTAINS")

        # ---- import edges ----
        for imp in rec.get("imports", []):
            module = imp.get("module") or imp.get("name") or ""
            if not module:
                continue
            target_id = _resolve_import(
                module, file_path, all_file_paths, repo_name
            )
            if target_id and target_id != fid:
                G.add_edge(fid, target_id, relation="IMPORTS", module=module)

    return G


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Serialisation helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def graph_to_dict(G: nx.DiGraph, repo_name: str) -> dict:
    """
    Convert the graph to a JSON-serialisable summary dict.

    Returns:
        {
            "repository": str,
            "summary":    { files, functions, classes, imports },
            "nodes":      [ {id, type, label, ...} ],
            "edges":      [ {source, target, relation} ]
        }
    """
    nodes = []
    for node_id, attrs in G.nodes(data=True):
        entry = {"id": node_id}
        entry.update(attrs)
        nodes.append(entry)

    edges = []
    for src, tgt, attrs in G.edges(data=True):
        entry = {"source": src, "target": tgt}
        entry.update(attrs)
        edges.append(entry)

    # Summary counts
    type_counts = {}
    for _, attrs in G.nodes(data=True):
        t = attrs.get("type", "unknown")
        type_counts[t] = type_counts.get(t, 0) + 1

    import_edges = [e for e in edges if e.get("relation") == "IMPORTS"]

    return {
        "repository": repo_name,
        "summary": {
            "files":     type_counts.get("file", 0),
            "functions": type_counts.get("function", 0),
            "classes":   type_counts.get("class", 0),
            "imports":   len(import_edges),
        },
        "nodes": nodes,
        "edges": edges,
    }


def graph_to_frontend_format(G: nx.DiGraph) -> dict:
    """
    Return a simplified nodes/edges dict suitable for D3 / react-force-graph.

    Nodes: { id, label, type }
    Edges: { source, target, label }
    """
    nodes = [
        {
            "id":    node_id,
            "label": attrs.get("label", node_id),
            "type":  attrs.get("type", "unknown"),
        }
        for node_id, attrs in G.nodes(data=True)
    ]

    edges = [
        {
            "source": src,
            "target": tgt,
            "label":  attrs.get("relation", ""),
        }
        for src, tgt, attrs in G.edges(data=True)
    ]

    return {"nodes": nodes, "edges": edges}
